cards.title: Compare different kinds of household pressure
cards.evidence: Debt / annualized disposable income: mortgage owners 306.1%; renters 56.4%.
cards.meaning: Debt relative to income and income relative to consumption measure different kinds of pressure.
cards.action: Review leverage and income relative to consumption separately.

cards.title: Positive saving can hide an income gap
cards.evidence: Income less consumption: CAD -572. Pension adjustment: CAD +841. Net saving: CAD +269.
cards.meaning: The pension adjustment changes the sign. Positive net saving does not mean income covered consumption.
cards.action: Show all three components before describing household saving.

cards.title: Payments rose while the ratio fell
cards.evidence: Ratio 14.52%. Payments +0.97%; income +2.06% quarter over quarter.
cards.meaning: Income grew faster than required payments. The lower ratio does not mean payments fell.
cards.action: Monitor payment growth alongside income growth.

cards.title: Complex models had higher average error
cards.evidence: Average absolute error: previous quarter 0.245; random forest 0.250; neural 0.387 percentage points.
cards.meaning: Lower error is better. The small sample does not establish a clear model advantage; the neural extension is exploratory.
cards.action: Keep the previous-quarter forecast as the benchmark.

scope: Public household group averages. They support reporting review and investigation, not individual default predictions. Group and national dates differ.
